doe-osti-2997045-transformational-nano-c:
GTI Energy's final report on award DE-FE0032215, issued 30 September 2025, covers a membrane meant to strip at least 97 percent of carbon dioxide from gas plant exhaust. Principal authors Shiguang Li of GTI Energy and Miao Yu, Fan Wang, and co-authors at the University at Buffalo worked from March 2023 to May 2025. Gas combined cycle exhaust is dilute, which makes capture costly.

The membrane traps an ionic liquid inside nanoscale pores, marrying liquid selectivity with a solid sheet's handling. Bench permeation runs show carbon dioxide flow falling steeply as its share in the feed rises, while nitrogen flow barely moves, so selectivity drops with richer feeds. A companion dehydration membrane handles the wet exhaust. The report records both the strong capture target and the feed effects a plant design must absorb.
nasa-tm-19680000663-review-of-nondestruc:
John A. Gibson, of the Battelle Memorial Institute in Columbus, Ohio, reviewed weld inspection methods in October 1967. The flaw in question is lack of penetration: a fusion weld that fails to join through the full thickness. His review covers butt joints in aluminum alloys welded from both sides.

A literature search tested how well standard methods find that flaw. Under some conditions, Gibson reports, ordinary ultrasonic and X-ray inspection may miss it. He reviews two improved X-ray approaches, including measuring density changes across the weld. Two ultrasonic upgrades also appear, one raising the test frequency. Some approaches plant an easy-to-see flaw that vanishes when penetration is complete.
